Compendium of Popular Medicine, Surgery, Ophthalmology, and Materia Medica for a Franciscan House in Austria or South Germany (c. 1675)

msContents.summary: Compendium of popular medicine and surgery, receipts, etc., in Early New High German (Austro-Bavarian dialect), compiled c. 1675 for a House of the Franciscan Order in Austria or South Germany. Pages 49–165 contain a specialized treatise on ophthalmology preceded on p. 48 (Canvas 25) by a multi-layered laminated anatomical flap dissection of the eye (photographed in lifted states on Canvases 727–730).
msContents.textLang: Early New High German (Austro-Bavarian dialect) with Latin anatomical and pharmaceutical terminology.

supportDesc.support: Laid paper with watermarks (documented in transmitted-light shots on Canvases 736–743).
supportDesc.extent: 1 volume: pp. [29], 30–790 + 4 index leaves, 4to (20.5 x 15 cm); 745 IIIF canvases.20.515.0

collation.p: Pages 1–28 (or 1–29 in catalogue, though unnumbered recto [p. 29] survives on Canvas 7), 56–59, 76, 77, 251, 252, 435–438, 484–487, 490–499, 652–659, 725, 762, 783–786 are wanting, as well as the end of the alphabetical index after the middle of letter P. A large piece is torn away from pp. 417/418 (Canvases 733–735). Pagination is irregular (e.g. p. 30 on verso Canvas 8 faces p. 32 on recto Canvas 9, skipping 31 without text loss).

layout.p: Written in double column within red rules (with occasional full-width single-column pages such as p. 49), headings and section rubrics in red ink.

handNote.p: Main 17th-century Austro-Bavarian scribal hand writing German Kurrentschrift for vernacular text, humanist cursiva antiqua for Latin technical terms, and red ink for rubrics and ruling.
20th-century bookseller and library cataloguer hands on pastedown and flyleaf 1r.

decoNote.p: Contains over 300 watercolour illustrations (including 15 nearly full-page paintings of Franciscan friar-surgeons, operations, laboratories, apothecary shops, instruments, and chemical apparatus), ~60 ophthalmic drawings on pp. 48–165, and a 3-layer movable anatomical eye flap on p. 48 (Canvas 25 + Canvases 727–730).

binding.p: Modern stamped brown morocco binding with gilt spine lettering: COMPENDIUM OF MEDICINE AND SURGERY / M. S. GERMAN. / CA 1650–1680 (Canvas 1, Canvas 722, Canvas 723).

history.acquisition: Purchased in 1922 from Gilhofer & Ranschburg, Vienna (600 Swiss francs / £24), Accession No. 41913.

editorialDecl.p:
Diplomatic transcription preserving original Early New High German spelling, vocalic diacritics, capitalization, punctuation, and lineation. Line breaks (
) and zones () are anchored to pixel coordinates (#xywh=x,y,w,h) on the Wellcome IIIF canvases.

zone.desc: Wellcome Historical Medical Library Bookplate (Acc. 41913, MS.990) — Printed red-and-black heraldic ex-libris of the Wellcome Historical Medical Library with manuscript blue-ink accession number '41913' and shelfmark 'MS.990'.

Watercolour Bust Portrait of a Gentleman in Red Doublet and Pleated Ruff (p. 32, Col. B Upper) — Half-column watercolour portrait showing a dark-haired, mustachioed man in a crimson doublet and broad scalloped lace-edged ruff Collar (representing a patient afflicted with oral/dental disease), bordered below by a double red-and-ochre rule.

Watercolour Study of Four Extracted Human Molar Teeth (p. 33, Col. B Middle) — Shaded watercolour anatomical illustration of four extracted human molars in lateral/oblique view, depicting crown cusps and bifurcated/trifurcated roots, above a double yellow-and-red horizontal rule.

Watercolour Illustration of a Spotted Frog ('Fröschel' / Ranula Visual Mnemonic, p. 35, Col. B Upper) — Watercolour painting of a brown-and-ochre spotted frog in dorsal view with four webbed feet, serving as a visual-etymological emblem for 'Fröschel vnder der Zungen' (Latin 'ranula', 'little frog', sublingual retention cyst/swelling), above a double yellow-ochre rule.

Watercolour Study of Four Single- and Multi-Rooted Human Teeth (p. 36, Col. A Upper) — Watercolour anatomical row of four extracted human teeth showing a single-rooted premolar, conical canine/incisor, bifurcated molar, and trifurcated molar above a double yellow-ochre rule.

Watercolour Profile Portrait of a Patient Using a Brass Oral Syringe (p. 36, Col. B Middle) — Watercolour half-length profile of a male patient wearing a striped cap and red tunic with a turned brass wound/oral syringe ('Einspritz-Spritze') inserted into his mouth, above a double yellow-ochre rule.

Portrait of a man with neckcloth — Watercolor and ink bust portrait of a mustachioed man wearing a dark brimmed cap/turban, a dark scarf/neckcloth wrapped around his throat, and a reddish-brown buttoned coat, illustrating the section on throat ailments (Angina).
Portrait of a young man in profile — Bust portrait in left profile of a young man with short brown hair wearing a yellow and green/grey striped collar/garment, above a horizontal rule.
Frontal portrait of a youth — Frontal bust portrait of a youth with curly brown hair wearing a red, green, and dark-striped collar/garment, above a horizontal rule.

Goitre Dialogue — Watercolor illustration of a man in a green turban and a woman with a braided headdress, both displaying large neck goitres and pointing at each other's swellings, with German caption above.
Facial Spots and Pustules — Watercolor illustration of a woman in a grey-blue headscarf and red-brown bodice, her face covered in small red-brown spots and pustules.
Fig. 1 (Ear abscess patient) — Bust of a young person in profile facing right, raising one hand to touch his cheek/ear area, above a framed ledge marked '1'.

Fig. 2 (Birthmark patients) — Front-facing bust of a woman with reddish-brown birthmarks on her forehead/right eye and under her left eye, wearing a headscarf, with a small child standing behind her left shoulder, above a framed ledge marked '||'.
Fig. 1 (Facial pimples/pustules patient) — Front-facing head of a woman wearing a light headscarf/bonnet, showing reddish spots/pimples on her cheeks and face, above a framed ledge marked '|||'.
State 1 (Flaps Closed): Outer Tunic F (Conjunctiva/Sclera with vascular arborization), Cornea G, Pupil H, Optic Stalk A/B/D/E.
State 2 (First Flap F Lifted): Reveals Optic Nerve Sheath K-K, Dark Choroid/Uvea Tunic I (with vascular arborization), and Pupil/Iris H/R.
State 3 (Second Flap I Lifted): Reveals Net-like Retina Tunic L (Tunica retiformis ò retina) enclosing the Vitreous Humor.
State 4 (Third Flap L Lifted — Deepest Interior): Reveals Optic Nerve Core m, Vitreous Humor n, Crystalline Lens o, and Aqueous Humor P.
Diagram A: Eye in its form with extraocular muscles elevated — Watercolour drawing of the eyeball ('A') with the rectus muscles splayed upward toward the optic apex.

Diagram A–I, a: Posterior/frontal stellate view of the six extraocular muscles, trochlea G, sclera H, optic nerve I, and motor nerve twigs a — Watercolour anatomical rosette showing muscles A–F radiating from globe H/I, pulley G on the superior oblique F, and nerve branches a.
Diagram B: Crystalline humor with the tunica aranea — Concentric circular watercolour diagram of the lens encircled by the arachnoid/ciliary membrane.
Diagram D: Crystalline humor bare and alone — Small circular watercolour diagram of the isolated crystalline lens ('D').
Diagram C: Posterior white vitreous humor with the crystalline lens — Crescentic watercolour diagram of the vitreous body ('C') cradling the spherical crystalline lens.

Laminated Multi-Layer Flap Dissection of the Eye (Labels A–R across 4 physical states, Canvases 25 & 727–730) — Interactive 3-flap watercolour anatomical cut-out pasted onto p. 48, lifting sequentially to reveal Tunica Conjunctiva/Cornea (F, G, H), Tunica Uvea/Choroid (I, K, R), Tunica Retina (L), and the internal humors (m, n, o, P).

Portrait of a Patient with Bilateral Cataracts (p. 52, Col. A Upper) — Half-column watercolour bust portrait of a young mustachioed man wearing a crimson cap with broad gold-ochre trim and a dark high-collared doublet, depicting pale, cloudy pupils characteristic of cataracts ('der Staan').

Portrait #1: Franciscan Friar with White Milky Cataracts (p. 54, Col. A Lower) — Half-column watercolour bust portrait labeled '#.1.' showing a bearded Franciscan friar in a brown hooded habit (cowl) with wide-open eyes and opaque white pupils illustrating the 'Weisen Milchstar' (milky cataract).

Figur: Patient Performing Ocular Steam Fumigation (p. 55, Col. A Lower) — Half-column watercolour illustration titled 'Figur Wie Man sich Zum Bähen Schikhen soll' showing a patient in a green coat with red cuffs and grey stockings leaning over a steaming earthenware pot on a yellow wooden table with a white linen cloth draped over the head to trap the herbal vapor.

Portrait No. 2: Patient with Gray Cataract (p. 60, Col. A Middle) — Half-column watercolour bust portrait labeled 'No. 2.' and titled 'Figur des Grauben Staan', depicting a curly-haired figure with light gray/ash-colored pupils.

Apparatus Diagram: Wick-Filtration / Decanting into Glass Flask (p. 60, Col. B Upper) — Watercolour laboratory diagram showing a cylindrical basin on a wooden block decanting green-tinted eye-water through a red felt strip ('filzl rodes düch') into a globular glass flask on a lower block.

Portrait No. 5: Patient with 'Bösen Mangel der Augen' (p. 62, Col. B Middle) — Half-column watercolour bust portrait labeled 'No. 5' and titled 'Figur des bösen Mangel der augen', showing a young figure with wavy brown hair, pale complexion, reddish sclera, and small constricted pupils ('eng und klein').

Portrait No. 6: Woman with 'Bössen Augen' (p. 63, Col. A Lower) — Half-column watercolour bust portrait labeled 'No 6.' and titled 'Die andre figur, der bössen augen', depicting a woman wearing a red-and-gold striped head-veil and a high yellow pleated collar, with slightly asymmetric, constricted pupils.

Portrait No. 4: Woman with Black Cataract / Gutta Serena (p. 64, Col. A Upper) — Half-column watercolour bust portrait labeled '4.to.' and titled 'Figur des Schwartzen Starn oder Gutta Serena', showing a woman wearing a green striped cap and yellow wimple with abnormally wide, dark pupils.

Portrait No. 3: Gentleman with Second Kind of Black Cataract (p. 65, Col. A Upper) — Half-column watercolour bust portrait labeled '3ti.' and titled 'Figur der andern ardt des Schwartzen Starn', showing a curly-haired, mustachioed man with a goatee in a dark high-collared doublet, exhibiting wide dark pupils.

Illustration: Five Apothecary Jars and Glass Flasks (p. 66, Col. A Middle) — Watercolour row of five pharmaceutical vessels resting on a shelf: three cylindrical terracotta/wooden albarelli (two open, one lidded) alternating with two square glass stoppered bottles.

Full-Page Illustration #7: Franciscan Friar Performing Cataract Couching (p. 70) — Full-page watercolour scene labeled '#.o 7.' showing three Franciscan friars in brown habits inside a room with diamond-tiled floor, leaded glass window, and heavy iron-hinged door: an assistant friar steadies the seated patient's head against his chest while the friar-oculist performs cataract couching in the right eye, beside a surgical table bearing spare needles, square compresses, a blue ointment/egg-white bowl, and a curved bandage.

Portrait #8: Couching Needle Inserted into Right Eye (p. 71, Col. A Lower) — Half-column watercolour portrait labeled '#8.' and titled 'Figur Wie man das Jnstrument in das aug sezt', showing a woman with golden-brown braided hair and a cataract needle inserted horizontally into the temporal sclera of her right eye.

Diagram #9: Three Cataract Couching Needles (p. 71, Col. B Upper) — Watercolour instrument plate labeled '#.o 9.' and titled 'Wie die Jnstrumendt oder Star Nadl Sein Sollen', depicting three couching needles: one with a plain turned handle and two with spiral-fluted handles and spherical pommels.

Diagram #10 (Upper): Pair of Round Flax/Tow Eye Pledgets (p. 73, Col. A Upper) — Watercolour diagram labeled '#.o 10.' and titled 'Figur dess flachs beischel', depicting two circular coiled brown flax/tow pads.
Diagram #10 (Lower): Pair of Square Linen-Backed Eye Pledgets (p. 73, Col. A Lower) — Watercolour diagram showing two round flax/tow pads mounted upon square linen cloth backing.

Portrait #11: Patient with Square Eye Pledgets Applied (p. 73, Col. B Middle) — Half-column watercolour bust portrait labeled '#.11.' showing a mustachioed man with square white-bordered brown flax pledgets covering both eyes.

Portrait #12: Patient Wearing Taffeta Eye-Shade Visor (p. 74, Col. B Upper) — Half-column watercolour portrait labeled '#12.' showing a curly-haired, mustachioed man wearing a yellow-green taffeta eye-shade visor tied across his forehead to shield his recovering eyes from bright light.

Portrait: Nun Demonstrating Lacrimal Fistula (p. 82, Col. B Middle) — Half-column watercolour bust portrait showing a nun in a black veil and white linen wimple pressing her right index finger against the inner canthus of her right eye, from which blood and purulent discharge trickle down beside her nose ('fistula Lacrimale').

Full-Width Operative Scene #1: Franciscan Friar Operating on a Nun's Lacrimal Fistula (p. 83) — Large watercolour surgical scene labeled '#.o 1.' showing a nun in white habit seated in an armchair with her wrists bound with red ribbons, blood streaming down her cheek from the right inner canthus, steadied by two nuns (one holding a crucifix) while a third nun looks in at the doorway and a bearded Franciscan friar stands before her holding a lancet and linen cloth next to a yellow instrument table.

Portrait #2: Nun After Lacrimal Fistula Incision (p. 84, Col. A Middle) — Half-column watercolour bust portrait labeled '#.2' depicting a nun in black veil and white wimple with fresh blood streaming from the incised right inner canthus.

Instrument Plate #3: Three Surgical Knives and Lancets (p. 84, Col. B Upper) — Watercolour instrument plate labeled '#.o 3.' illustrating three surgical blades: a curved sickle-shaped bistoury with red gold-flecked handle, a folding lancet in an ornate red-and-gold sheath, and a straight scalpel with red gold-flecked handle.
Instrument #4 (Upper): Curved Actual Cautery Iron (p. 84, Col. B Lower) — Watercolour drawing labeled '#.o 4.' depicting an iron cautery with a curved/cupped tip and turned wooden handle.

Instrument #4 (Lower): Protective Metal Eye-Shield (p. 84, Col. B Bottom) — Watercolour drawing labeled '#.o 4.' showing a contoured metal protective eye-shield with a central arched bridge to guard the eyeball from heat during cauterization.

Instrument Plate #5: Three Lacrimal Cautery Irons (p. 85, Col. A Upper) — Watercolour instrument plate labeled '#.o 5.' depicting three iron actual cauteries with spherical/button tips (two curved, one straight) and carved brown wooden handles.

Instrument Plate #6: Three Spiral Bone Drills / Perforators (p. 87, Col. B Lower) — Watercolour instrument plate labeled '#.o 6.' and titled 'Form vnd gestalt der Jnstrument Zum durch born', illustrating three long metal bone-drills with spiral auger tips and turned wooden handles.

Operative Scene: Franciscan Surgeon and Nuns Attending Post-Trephining Patient (p. 88) — Large watercolour scene in an infirmary chamber with leaded window and yellow curtain: on the left, the Franciscan friar-surgeon stands with his back turned at a yellow surgical table laid with knives, forceps, and flasks; at center-right, a nun in brown habit sits bound in an armchair with a bleeding right inner canthus, supported by a second nun behind her, while another nun stands weeping/dabbing her own eye with a cloth and a fourth nun enters the doorway holding a yellow flask.

Portrait A: Man in Red Cap with Corneal Film (p. 89, Col. B Upper) — Half-column watercolour bust portrait labeled '.A.' showing a mustachioed man wearing a red knit cap, looking downward/aside with cloudy corneal opacities.

Portrait B: Gentleman with Bilateral Corneal Films (p. 89, Col. B Lower) — Half-column watercolour bust portrait labeled '.B.' showing a curly-haired, mustachioed man with a goatee and pale gray films ('Bladter fell') across both eyes.

Illustration: Three Blue-and-White Apothecary Jars (p. 92, Col. A Upper) — Watercolour drawing of three bulbous blue-and-white striped ceramic apothecary albarelli/jars covered with parchment/cloth caps on a yellow shelf.

Illustration: Hard-Boiled Egg for Eye-Water Preparation (p. 92, Col. B Upper) — Watercolour drawing of an oval white-and-grey shaded egg resting on a golden surface, illustrating the 'Augen Wasser Von airn' recipe.

Portrait C: Young Woman Illustrating 'Waser Fell' (p. 95, Col. B Upper) — Half-column watercolour bust portrait labeled '.C.' and titled 'Figur der Waser fell', showing a young woman wearing a red headdress with green foliage, a pearl drop earring, a red-beaded necklace, and a pale watery swelling on her eyes.

Illustration: Patient Seated in Armchair for Pterygium Surgery (p. 97, Col. B Upper) — Half-column watercolour figure showing a mustachioed man wearing a buttoned white doublet, green knee-breeches, white stockings, and black buckled shoes seated upright in a red-backed wooden armchair.

Portrait D: Patient with Vascular 'Fleisch Fell' / Pterygium (p. 98, Col. A Upper) — Half-column watercolour bust portrait labeled '.D.' and titled 'Figur der fleisch fell', depicting a curly-haired, mustachioed man in a brown-and-gold collar with reddened eyes and vascular fleshy growths.

Portrait E: Young Woman Illustrating 'Mukh Maill' / Fly-Spot (p. 99, Col. A Middle) — Half-column watercolour bust portrait labeled '.E.' and titled 'Figur der Mukh Maill', showing a young woman with braided brown hair, a green leaf ornament on the left, and a red ribbon tied at her throat.

Portrait F: Woman with Hot Weeping Ocular Fluxes (p. 100, Col. A Upper) — Half-column watercolour bust portrait labeled '.F.' depicting a curly-haired woman with a gold neckband, intensely reddened conjunctivae, and tear streaks running down both cheeks.

Illustration: Three Brass Vessels for Eye-Water Preparation (p. 103, Col. B Upper) — Watercolour drawing of one large central brass vessel flanked by two smaller brass bowls/cups resting on a wooden shelf, illustrating the brass-vessel beating of sal ammoniac and egg-white collyria.

Portrait .G.: Woman with Cold Weeping Eye Fluxes (p. 105, Col. A) — Watercolour bust portrait labeled '.G.' depicting a woman in a blue headscarf with white under-cap and grey-brown cloak, weeping watery tears from both eyes.

Portrait .H.: Man with Chronic Evil Eye Fluxes (p. 106, Col. B) — Watercolour bust portrait labeled '.H.' depicting a curly-haired man with moustache and goatee in a grey cloak, weeping dark tears from both eyes.

Instrument Plate .I.: Seton Clamp, Needle, and Red Silk Cord (p. 107, Col. A) — Full-column watercolour instrument plate labeled '.I.' depicting the steel seton screw-clamp with a pointed needle passed through its lower jaws and a long twisted red crimson silk cord.

Portrait .K.: Patient with Seton Clamp and Red Cord in Nape (p. 108, Col. A) — Watercolour profile portrait labeled '.K.' showing a curly-haired man with weeping right eye, with the steel seton clamp gripping the nape of his neck and the red silk cord passing through.

Portrait .L.: Woman with Penetrating Eye Injury (p. 109, Col. B) — Watercolour profile portrait labeled '.L.' depicting a woman with a blue hair ribbon, red coral earring, and red coral necklace, with a small knife piercing her left eye and blood flowing down her cheek.

Portrait .M.: Figure Wearing Dark-Rimmed Spectacles (p. 112, Col. A) — Watercolour bust portrait labeled '.M.' depicting a person wearing a yellow-orange patterned cap and dark-rimmed nose-bridge spectacles.
Ash-Wood Drinking Cup (p. 113, Col. A) — Small inline watercolour illustration of a yellow wooden cup/beaker turned by a cooper from ash wood ('Von Eschig').

Figure .N.: Patient Receiving Celandine Steam via Bifurcated Funnel (p. 116, Col. B) — Watercolour scene labeled '.N.' showing a curly-haired man in a yellow coat and green stockings leaning over a wooden table, holding a green bifurcated funnel over an earthenware pot to channel herbal steam into both eyes.

Instrument Plate .O.: Bifurcated Eye-Steaming Funnel (p. 117, Col. A) — Standalone watercolour instrument illustration labeled '.O.' under 'Figur des Instruments', depicting a green glass conical base splitting into two narrow eye-cups.

Portrait .P.: Youth with Purulent Eye Discharge (p. 118, Col. B) — Watercolour bust portrait labeled '.P.' depicting a curly-haired young person in a brown collar with greyish purulent matter streaming from both eyes.
Nun with inflamed eyes — Half-length/bust watercolour illustration of a nun in a black veil and white wimple with markedly reddened, inflamed eyes.

Portrait of a man with unnatural redness of the eyes — Bust portrait in watercolor of a mustachioed man wearing a yellow cap with red plume and a green coat with pink collar, depicting bloodshot, inflamed sclerae to illustrate 'unnatural redness of the eyes' (Von Vnnatirlichen Röde der augen).

Portrait of a nun with bloodshot eyes — Front-facing bust illustration in ink and watercolor of a nun wearing a black veil, white wimple, and brown habit, with visibly reddened, bloodshot eyes illustrating subconjunctival hemorrhage.

Three eye probes / blunt-ended needles — Three horizontal yellow-tinted ink-and-wash drawings of smooth, blunt-ended or knobbed surgical probes/needles ('glates khnäpfel') used to sweep under the eyelid to remove foreign bodies.

.F. — Watercolor illustration of a female patient's head in a red headscarf/veil, showing two circular flesh-colored ocular growths/excisions hanging from the eyes with red silk sutures and blood streaks.
Surgical needles — Two curved surgical needles (one threaded with red silk) drawn below the patient portrait.

Surgical illustration of eyelid incision and bleeding — Watercolor portrait of a young person's head with shoulder-length curly brown hair, facing forward. Vertical red streaks of blood drip from both lower eyelids down the cheeks. A dark curved surgical needle or lancet is positioned at the upper margin of the patient's left eye (viewer's right), illustrating the suturing and excision of the eyelid.

Vesicatoria behind the ears — Watercolor illustration of the back of a man's curly brown head showing two rectangular white blistering plasters (vesicatoria) applied behind the left and right ears, bounded below by a red horizontal rule.

Closed eyelids of a woman — Watercolor portrait of a woman's face with closed eyes, dark curly hair adorned with red ribbons/bows, and a gold band and red bead necklace, illustrating fused/closed eyelids above a red horizontal dividing rule.

Excision of eyelid growths — Watercolor portrait of a mustachioed and goateed man's face with two large round reddish growths protruding from both eyelids, each pierced by suture threads and dripping blood down his cheeks, bounded below by a red-orange horizontal rule.

Eye Stye / Hordeolum Portrait — Watercolor portrait of a man with brown curly hair, stylized black geometric moustache and goatee patches, and swollen reddish upper eyelids illustrating eye styes ('gersten oder habern').

Figur der Waser Gall — Watercolor portrait of a man with brown curly hair, thin moustache and goatee, displaying two large round fluid-filled swellings ('water galls' / atheromata) on both upper eyelids.

Apothecary Eye Dispensary — Full-page coloured pen-and-ink wash illustration framed by two blue marbled columns and a yellow-and-grey stone arch. Five yellow shelves hold rows of apothecary vessels under hanging signs: Augen Pilule (11 red cylindrical jars), Augen Puluer (10 red jars), Augen salben (8 blue-and-white ceramic albarelli), Augen waser (7 square glass bottles), and Augen Confect (12 red jars). Below, a tonsured Franciscan friar in a brown habit with a rosary hands a small bottle to a blindfolded gentleman holding a hat and walking stick, while two more blindfolded patients with sticks enter through a doorway on the left. A framed chart hangs on the back wall and a table on the right holds apothecary vessels.
Two Pillboxes — Coloured pen-and-ink wash illustration on a yellow background band showing two round ribbed wooden or earthenware pillboxes filled with dark spherical pills.

Five Eye-Water Flasks — Row of five rectangular/octagonal colored apothecary bottles or flasks with stoppers (reddish-purple, blue, pink, tan, dark blue-green) standing on a brown shelf beneath the heading for various eye waters.

Four Apothecary Ointment Jars — Watercolor illustration of four apothecary jars/pots arranged in a row on a brown shelf: from left to right, a white/grey bulbous jar, a reddish-brown jar, a yellow-ochre lidded jar, and a pinkish-red handled pitcher.
Fig. 1 — Watercolor drawing in a rectangular ink frame depicting a human eye with a brown iris and a white spot/opacity (fell/fleck) on the cornea/pupil.

Fig. 2 — Full-width watercolor scene depicting a bearded friar/monk surgeon in a brown habit performing an eye operation with a small instrument on a male patient in a blue coat and red breeches lying on a wooden bench/bed. To the left is an apothecary shelf with red jars, colored glass bottles, and a table with flasks; behind is an open wooden door and a leaded-glass window on the right.

Ophthalmic probes and specula/applicators — Three horizontal instrument drawings in the upper left column: (1) a brown rod with a stippled, round sponge- or brush-like head at the left end; (2) a brown rod with a similar stippled round head at the right end; (3) a blue-grey double-ended probe/cannula with two small blue-grey eyed/ringed instruments (possibly eye specula or trocars/guards) drawn directly beneath it.

Masticatory lozenges / troches — Three circular golden-brown lozenges or troches drawn in a row below the opening continuation lines in the left column; the first two show six-spoked wheel/star markings, while the third is plain stippled brown-gold.

Sief collyria forms (cones and discs) — Eight dark grey-brown drawings of Sief collyria/troches arranged in a horizontal row above the 'Sief' rubric in the right column: three pointed cones on the left, three circular discs in the middle, and two pointed cones on the right.
Apothecary Ointment Jar — Coloured drawing of a blue-grey glazed ceramic apothecary jar resting on a yellow/ochre oval base at the top of the right column.
Bandaged Head — Coloured drawing of a young person's head with curled hair and a blue cloth bandage tied around the forehead with a bow on the left, above a horizontal scroll/bar.
Green Cylindrical Apothecary Jar — Coloured drawing of a green cylindrical apothecary vessel/jar resting on a yellow/ochre oval base in the lower left column.

Two men gesturing in conversation — Colored watercolor/ink illustration at top left above the title: on the left, a man in a white cap and beige/brown robe gesturing toward the right; on the right, a man in a red plumed hat, yellow doublet, and blue breeches gesturing toward the left, standing on grassy ground.

Upper-Left Distillation Vessels — Three vessels: a round-bottomed flask seated in a cylindrical vessel with radiating lines at top; a blue-tinted glass retort/alembic with side spout; and a blue-tinted two-handled circulatory vessel (pelican).

Upper-Right Serpentine Distillation Train — Brown earthenware cucurbit with a tall zigzag/serpentine ascending condenser column and alembic head discharging into a tilted blue glass receiver set in a funnel-topped pedestal, fed simultaneously by a tall blue-tinted matrass-alembic on the right.

Middle-Left Tripod Vat and Crossed-Spout Alembics — At left, a three-legged stand over a small blue flask and fire supporting a coopered vat, cloth strainer, and top dish of red-orange coals/herbs with a long handle; at right, two blue glass alembics with crossed spouts.

Middle-Right Conical Hood and Bath-Seated Vessel — At left, a horizontal conical blue glass hood/funnel with two spouts; at right, a faceted blue glass vessel seated inside a round brown earthenware bath dish.

Lower-Left Brick Furnace and Circulatory Flask — At left, a brick-built furnace with arched firebox heating a bath and blue glass alembic whose spout drains into a small receiver on an adjacent plinth; at right, a tall pear-shaped blue glass matrass/circulatory flask.

Lower-Right Brick Furnace with Stool-Mounted Receiver — A brick furnace with arched firebox heating a copper/brown retort whose spout leads into a brown earthenware receiver jar resting on a four-legged wooden stool, with a small pot beneath.

Upper-Left Alembic in Bath and Earthenware Retort — At left, a blue glass alembic seated in a yellow-brown bath ring; at right, a large brown earthenware retort with long curving neck discharging into a blue glass long-necked receiver.

Upper-Right Spigoted Condenser Vat and Receivers — A large copper/brown funnel-shaped vat with a side spigot mounted atop a two-handled brown earthenware jug; a tilted blue glass flask on a tall wooden stand feeds in at left, while a tall blue-grey two-handled amphora catches the outflow at right.

Middle-Left Stepped Cascade, Double Pot, and Bath Flask — A five-tier brick stepped cascade with cups linked by red overflow tubes into a tilted glass flask; a two-part brown earthenware stacked vessel (aludel/digestion pot) at right; and a pear-shaped spouted vessel in a yellow-brown bath ring below.

Middle-Right Multi-Bulbed Column and Paired Alembics — Three blue-tinted glass vessels: a four-bulbed fractionating/aludel column with alembic head at left, a pear-shaped alembic in the center, and a conical-bodied alembic at right with crossing spouts.

Lower-Left Brick Furnace with Wooden Cooling Barrel — A square brick furnace with arched firebox and square vent topped by a dark copper still whose long spout passes through a coopered wooden cooling barrel (worm tub) on a four-legged stand.

Lower-Right Stepped Cascade and Gourd Vessel — At left, a three-tier brick stepped cascade with shallow bowls linked by red overflow streams into a small tilted glass receiver; at right, a tall double-bellied brown earthenware gourd-shaped vessel.

Double-alembic water/sand-bath furnace — Watercolor illustration of a cylindrical brick furnace on three legs with a square fire-door, topped by a round wooden-staved bath vessel holding two blue-gray alembics/retorts with spouts.

Barrel-bath alembic furnace — Watercolor illustration of a square/box-like furnace base supporting a cylindrical bath and a wooden-staved barrel vessel containing a blue-gray cucurbit and alembic head.

Brick retort/alembic furnace with receiver — Watercolor illustration of a rectangular brick furnace with an arched fire-door, topped by a blue-gray alembic whose spout leads into a tilted blue-gray receiver flask resting on a four-legged wooden stand.

Surgical and medical instruments plate — Full-page watercolor illustration arranged in two vertical zones: left side with curved handle/saw frame, two blades with folding wooden handle, large surgical shears/forceps, awl/trocar, cylindrical case, fine probes/needles, tenaculum hook, and long rod with floral/sponge head; right side with cupping cylinder and funnel, long catheter/syringe probe, S-curved speculum/forceps with turned wooden handle, large S-curved metal pipe/flask, square bottle with needle, and two long cautery rods with turned wooden handles.

Sickroom scene — Watercolor illustration spanning the full page width: a bare-chested bearded patient under a green blanket in a carved wooden bed on the left; a long-haired physician gesturing between the patient and a standing weeping woman holding a handkerchief to her eyes; a green-draped table with vessels and plates, a four-paned window, and an open wooden door on the right.

Varicose Veins (Krampfadern) Illustration — Watercolor and ink anatomical illustration of a seated figure's lower body in yellow breeches with bare legs, showing prominent, tortuous, dark red-purple varicose veins (Krampfadern) along the calves and shins, resting on a horizontal ground line.

Sickbed Nursing Scene — Watercolor illustration in a black-ruled frame showing a bearded, tonsured friar in a brown habit lying in a wooden bed under a white coverlet. Beside the bed is a small wooden chair with a heart-shaped cutout, and behind it a table with an hourglass, a book, a crucifix, apothecary jars, and a cup. On the right, a second friar enters through an open doorway carrying a white-draped tray with a pitcher and five bowls.

Wie man die khranckhe in fieber mit Essen vnd Trinckhen halten Soll — Framed watercolor illustration showing a bearded man in a brown robe seated at a wooden table in a room with a framed picture on the wall. On the table are plates of food, bread, a knife, and a pewter pitcher and cup.
Illustration 1 (Canvas 154) — A pointing hand (manicule) with a dark cuff drawn in ink and wash in the upper left column, pointing right toward the first fever plaster recipe.

Illustration 2 (Canvas 154) — A shaded ink-and-wash drawing of a round-bellied pitcher/jug with a handle and a small loaf or stone beside it, placed to the left of the rubric 'in den fieber Solle das ordinari Trankh sein volgents'.

Illustration 1 (Canvas 155) — A small shaded ink-and-wash drawing of a round-bellied jug/pitcher with a handle in the upper left margin beside the rubric 'Waßer für das ordinari Trankh in Jeden fieber'.

dies Critici. 7. 14. 21. 27. / dies Decretorej. 4. 9. 14. 17. 21. 23. 27. — A framed colored ink-and-wash illustration in the lower left showing an elderly or sickly figure wearing a white headwrap, dark cloak with a yellow collar, and long reddish-brown skirt, leaning on a walking stick indoors beside a wooden door.

Illustration of the coronal suture on the head (adjacent to 'Volgenter Sÿrup ist sehr khöstlich') — Pen-and-ink and watercolor wash drawing of a human head tilted slightly forward, with brown curly hair, downcast eyes, nose, and mouth. Red lines mark a horizontal band around the forehead/temples intersecting a vertical line along the sagittal suture at a small red circle on the coronal suture ('Commissura Coronale'), illustrating the site of application referenced in the text above.

Illustration of a patient with petechiae in bed — Framed rectangular watercolor showing a bearded male patient propped up on white pillows in a wooden bed under a white sheet, bare-chested with red petechial spots on his torso and arms, wearing a red headband and holding a long black-and-gold rosary; to the right stands a female attendant in a purplish-pink dress and dark cap holding a shallow brown basin, with a table bearing a bowl of red fruit in the background.

Bedside scene of a fever patient, physician, and grieving woman — A central watercolor illustration showing a bare-chested patient with wavy brown hair sitting propped up on white pillows in a wooden bed under a white sheet and mottled rose-red coverlet. To the right, a physician in a black skullcap, white collar, and fur-trimmed robe rests his right hand on the patient's shoulder while pointing with his left toward a wooden table beneath a four-paned window; on the table stand a small crucifix, apothecary jars and flasks (containing yellow and pink liquids), and a bowl with a spoon. On the far left, a woman in a red bodice and white skirt stands in an open doorway, holding a cloth to her face in grief.

Fumigation censer (bottom left) — A footed chalice-like censer or brazier resting on a yellow base, filled with glowing red-orange coals and herbs, with grey smoke billowing upward and a small ladle or pestle resting against the left side.

Man vomiting into a tub (middle right) — A bearded man in a grey tunic leaning forward over a round, banded wooden or ceramic tub, vomiting a stream of yellow-red bilious matter into the vessel while holding its rim.

Portrait of a youth with a cheek swelling — Framed watercolor bust portrait in the upper-middle left column depicting a young man with dark curly hair facing forward, showing a prominent, rounded, inflamed red swelling on his left cheek (malar/parotid region), illustrating the section on facial, ear, and cheek swellings.
Human Eye — Square framed watercolor illustration in the top-left corner depicting a single human eye with brown iris and eyelids, accompanying the section 'Augen schmerzen' (Eye Pains).

Youth with Nosebleed — Framed watercolor illustration in the bottom-left corner depicting a young man in profile wearing a yellow-brown garment, leaning forward with blood streaming from his nose into a small bowl held beneath his chin, accompanying the section 'Von Nasen. Fluetten' (Of Nosebleeds).

Zu der 11 sagen — Colored ink and watercolor illustration on the left side of the page showing a nude youth wearing a red cap, seated on a rectangular block in an outdoor landscape, with red spots and pustules (petechiae/pox) distributed across his chest, arms, legs, and face.

Portrait of a bearded man — Ink and wash bust portrait in the upper-left corner of the left column, depicting a bearded man with a tonsure or skullcap wearing a brown habit or robe, framed within a red-ruled border.

Illustration 1 (Canvas 193) — Colored ink and wash anatomical illustration in the lower left column depicting a bare-chested man wearing a yellow-ochre cap with brown trim, using both hands to pull open a diamond-shaped incision in his chest, exposing the red heart, lungs, and ribcage.

Illustration above 'Von Bluet speiben' (f. 228v, upper left) — Colored ink and watercolor illustration depicting a woman in 17th-century attire (headscarf/cap with red ribbons, yellow bodice over a white chemise, red skirt) leaning forward and holding a dark ceramic bowl into which she is spitting/vomiting a stream of bright red blood.

Fluß Chatar — Watercolor and ink illustration of a figure wearing a white linen cloth draped like a tent over the head and shoulders, wearing a red bodice and white sleeves, leaning over an ochre table to inhale vapors rising from a dark footed brazier or chafing dish filled with glowing coals and medicinal substances.

Von Großen Durst. — Ink and watercolor illustration of a woman in profile facing left, wearing a red bodice with white sleeves and a yellow-trimmed headdress, holding a large grey pewter or silver pitcher to her mouth with both hands to drink, standing on a green ground.
Illustration 1 (Canvas 203) — Watercolor illustration of a red anatomical heart positioned above a rectangular ink-drawn frame at the top of the left column.

Illustration 1 (Canvas 204) — Large watercolor illustration of an anatomical heart oriented horizontally with its apex pointing left, located in the lower-left quadrant beside the treatise on heart palpitation.

Illustration 1 (Canvas 207) — Hand-colored gouache/watercolor sickbed scene in the upper left column: a pale, bearded patient lies propped up in a wooden bed under white-and-blue-shaded sheets. Below the scene is a blank rectangular cartouche framed in gold.

Blank cartouche beneath profile portrait of a man — Watercolour and ink profile portrait facing left of a man with curly brown hair, a dark upturned moustache, and a small chin beard, set against a pale blue wash above an empty rectangular cartouche.

Man lying prostrate in a landscape — Watercolour and ink illustration showing a bearded man in a red coat/tunic, dark breeches, and black shoes lying supine on grassy green ground with a winding path and dark green trees/bushes in the background.

Illustration 1 (Canvas 214) — Red-wash anatomical illustration of the human stomach at the top of the left column, showing the esophagus entering from the upper right and the duodenum/pylorus curving to the upper left, set above a blank yellow-bordered cartouche.

Illustration of a vomiting patient — A colored pen-and-ink and watercolor illustration at the top of the left column. A woman in a green bodice and red skirt holds a basin while a man in a yellow doublet and red breeches leans forward and vomits into it. An animal (a pig or dog) stands on the right near a grassy mound, with an empty olive-bordered banner beneath the scene.
Pfordt Adern — Watercolor illustration in upper-left margin showing a reddish-brown branching vascular tree representing the portal vein system.
Nabel Adern — Watercolor illustration in lower-left margin showing reddish-brown branching umbilical vessels descending to a pale oval bladder-like organ.
Von der Lungel — Watercolor illustration in upper-center showing the trachea (windpipe) descending into lobed pinkish-brown lungs.
Herz Heisel oder Pericartio — Watercolor illustration in middle-center showing a pale conical pouch representing the pericardium.
Herz — Watercolor illustration in lower-center showing a reddish-brown heart with yellowish-brown surface vessels/fat.
Herz Khamer — Watercolor illustration in middle-left showing a reddish-brown cross-section of the heart with two V-shaped ventricular chambers.
Thürlein des Herzen — Watercolor illustration in lower-left showing a reddish-brown cross-section of the heart's two chambers and valve structures.
Herz Bladt Diaphragma — Watercolor illustration in upper-right showing a reddish-brown arched/domed diaphragm with small circular openings.
Leber — Watercolor illustration in middle-right showing a reddish-brown liver with branching grey-white vessels and a small green gallbladder at the lower edge.
Gall — Watercolor illustration in lower-right showing a yellowish-green elongated pear-shaped gallbladder and cystic duct.
Magen (Stomach) — Greyish-brown ink-and-wash drawing of the stomach pouch showing the esophageal and pyloric openings.

Ritzel (Pancreas) — Elongated tan-brown anatomical drawing of the pancreas with branching ducts or vessels extending downward.

Gekröß / Mesenterio (Mesentery) — Circular anatomical illustration showing the grey-shaded coiled intestine surrounding a yellow-ochre mesentery with a dense network of branching red-brown mesenteric vessels and two main upper trunks.

das Nötz / omentum (Omentum) — Yellowish-tan pouch-like anatomical drawing of the greater omentum with fine branching red-brown blood vessels.
Peritonea (Peritoneum) — Grey-shaded shield-shaped anatomical drawing of the peritoneum showing the central umbilicus (navel) and branching vessels.

Figur Und Verzaichnus der Bluet adern (Bloodletting Man / Aderlassmann) — Full-length colored ink-and-wash illustration of a standing male figure with long wavy brown hair and a white loincloth, standing on grassy ground, marked with capital letters (A, D, FE, H, L, M) indicating bloodletting veins.

114 / Vena Pulsatilis Arteria — Full-length frontal anatomical drawing in red ink depicting the human arterial tree, showing the aortic arch, carotid and brachial arteries, descending aorta with intercostal/visceral branches, and iliac/femoral arteries.

Figur der Vena Caua. oder Bluet ader Samen — Full-body schematic anatomical drawing in red-brown ink depicting the venous system (Vena Cava) branching from the central trunk into the head, arms, torso, liver/kidneys, and legs. Von ader lasen. Wan Man Lasen Soll — Watercolor and ink illustration at the top of the left column depicting a figure with wavy brown hair and a grey-blue tunic seated behind a wooden table. Human figure surrounded by the four elemental symbols — Circular watercolor and ink illustration in the upper left column showing a standing nude human figure wearing a white loincloth inside a blue-shaded sphere, flanked at the four corners outside the circle by the alchemical triangles for Air (upper left), Fire (upper right), Water (lower left), and Earth (lower right).

Portrait of a sanguine person — Hand-colored ink and wash bust portrait in the lower left column depicting a young person with shoulder-length wavy light-brown hair, rosy cheeks, red lips, and bare shoulders, illustrating the sanguine complexion.

Von der Complexion der Melancholia. — Coloured portrait bust of a woman representing the melancholic complexion (Melancholia) in the upper half of the right column, framed by a black horizontal rule below. Drawing of a handled flask (matula) — A small, lightly shaded ink/pencil sketch of a round-bellied glass vessel or urinal with a handle on the right, placed in the upper-middle of the right column alongside text discussing the expulsion of excess water/moisture in old age.

Figure of the Natural Spirits (Spiritus Naturales) — Full-length standing human figure stippled in yellow/ochre dots with arms slightly outstretched, depicting a dark reddish-brown organ in the upper abdomen.
Figure of the Vital Spirits (Spiritus Vitales) — Full-length standing human figure stippled in red dots with arms slightly outstretched, depicting a prominent red heart in the center of the chest.

Full-length anatomical figure with outstretched arms — A standing, frontal nude human figure rendered in grey-blue and greenish watercolor wash with ink outlines and subtle yellow-gold highlights on the hands and chest, with arms extended horizontally and palms open.

Portrait bust of a curly-haired youth — A watercolor and ink illustration of the head and neck of a young person with golden-brown curly hair looking slightly downward, illustrating the seat of the internal senses, imagination, and reason in the head.
Two hourglass symbols — Two side-by-side red-ink hourglass figures drawn beneath the rubric on the diurnal movement of the four humors, symbolizing the measurement of the six-hour humoral periods.

Upper 24-hour planetary and zodiacal wheel — Large concentric circular table divided into 24 hourly sectors (numbered 12, 1–11, 12, 1–11) with time-of-day labels ('Mitag', 'nach mitag', 'Undergang', 'miternacht', 'nach miternacht', 'Vormitag') around the perimeter and seven concentric rings pairing planetary glyphs with zodiacal signs.

Melancolia. hipocontrica. — Coloured ink and wash illustration of a melancholic man wearing a dark cap, a rose-red capelet over an ochre robe, holding a staff in his right hand and a celestial globe mounted on a golden chalice-like stand in his left hand; behind him is a four-paned window overlooking a starry night sky with a crescent moon.

Four apothecary or drinking vessels on a shelf — A colored watercolor illustration in the right column depicting four vessels resting on a brown wooden shelf or table: a brown striped beaker, a blue-and-white ceramic pitcher with a handle, a blue-and-white stemmed goblet, and a small brown bowl.

Three red-filled vessels on a tray — Small hand-colored illustration at the top left of the page beside the heading 'Absiesung des gebliedts', depicting three round golden-rimmed bowls or cupping vessels filled with a bright red substance (symbolizing blood) resting on a rectangular tan/wooden shelf or tray.

Patient suffering from belly flux — Watercolor illustration in the middle of the right column showing a figure dressed in a red tunic sitting barefoot on a round close-stool or pot outdoors on green ground with distant trees, illustrating lientery or belly flux.

Man squatting with rectal prolapse — Coloured pen-and-ink drawing at the top of the left column showing a man in a blue-grey tunic squatting on a green-yellow grassy hillock, illustrating rectal prolapse, above a horizontal rectangular frame.

Man hunched with colic pain — Coloured pen-and-ink drawing in the lower right column showing a standing man in a reddish-brown coat, yellow breeches, and green stockings, hunched forward clutching his abdomen in pain, on a grassy hillock above a rectangular frame.

Illustration on canvas 322 — Full-page colored illustration of an apothecary workshop. On the right, two tonsured friars in brown habits converse with him, one holding a small vial and handing over a written prescription (℞). On the checkered floor in the lower right sits a brick distillation furnace with glass retorts.

Illustration on canvas 324 — Small marginal ink-and-wash drawing in the right margin beside lines 22–24 depicting a cylindrical ribbed earthen vessel (haffen) and its domed lid (deckhel) for luting and reverberating the antimony powder.

Clyster syringe — Pen-and-ink and watercolor illustration of a yellow-brown cylindrical clyster syringe with a detached pointed nozzle on the left and a plunger handle on the right, resting above a narrow strip of green grass.

Three apothecary vessels on a wooden shelf (Left Column) — Colored pen-and-ink drawing depicting two cylindrical shaded beakers/tumblers and one handled pitcher/jug resting on a tan wooden ledge above the heading 'Emulsian oder Melaun Milch'.

Goblet with red wine and cylindrical jar on a shelf (Right Column) — Colored pen-and-ink drawing depicting a stemmed glass goblet filled with dark red liquid beside a cylindrical grey jar/box on a tan and reddish-brown shelf above the heading 'Von Ender hierlichen Wein'.

Illustration on canvas 366 — Small ink drawing of a pointing hand (manicule) with a cuff in the top-left margin beside the page number 402, pointing right toward the rubricated heading 'Pillule für Lienteria oder Weisse rüehr.'.

Four apothecary jars on a shelf — Watercolor illustration at the top of the left column depicting four red cylindrical apothecary vessels/jars with rims standing in a row on a brown shelf against a plain background.
Leaping stag — Hand-colored ink and watercolor illustration of a brown stag with antlers leaping to the left across green grassy terrain, framed below by a red ink horizontal line.

Distillation apparatus and furnace — Hand-colored ink and watercolor illustration of an alchemical distillation setup: a brick furnace on the right topped with a copper alembic whose spout leads to a large brown receiver vessel resting on a wooden stand on the left, with a small black pot underneath and a building with a smoking chimney in the background.

Apothecary grinding a substance on a stone slab — Color ink and wash illustration in the upper left column depicting a man in a green coat and brown breeches standing at a wooden table, grinding a red substance on a flat white stone slab with a muller held in both hands, with stylized grass and shrubs in the background.

Distillation apparatus — Colored drawing of a brick distillation furnace with an open firebox showing red flames, surmounted by a metallic or grey alembic with a long descending spout leading into a spherical glass receiver resting on a low four-legged stand.
Rose plant (Rosa) — Colored botanical illustration of a rose stem with green leaves, a small red bud, and a large pink-and-white double rose flower.

Bryonia (Prijonia) root — Hand-colored botanical watercolor and ink illustration at the top of the left column depicting a large yellow-ochre tuberous taproot with three green leafy stems.

Apothecary's workshop with monk — Full-page watercolor and ink illustration depicting four shelves of green, yellow, and terracotta apothecary jars above a leaded window, a yellow wall cabinet with black hinges, and a bearded monk in a brown habit holding a small red flask behind a red-draped table with a brass mortar and pestle, glass vials, and boxes; a distillation vessel sits at far left, and a large blank paper patch covers the lower-right half.

Distillation vessel (gläßl) for separating essential oils from water — Watercolor and ink illustration of a round blue-gray glass flask/receiver resting on a brownish-green mound with small yellow plant tufts, showing a narrow neck with a small attached side-receptacle or stopper at the top.

Wie Man den Terpenthin Leütern sol (Turpentine Purification Vessel) — Colored ink and wash illustration in the upper-middle of the right column depicting a golden-yellow cylindrical linden-wood container (Pixen) resting atop a grey-blue cylindrical receiving vessel/glass on a brown wooden block, illustrating the filtration of turpentine.
Rose blossom (Rosen Tinctur / Rosen Hönig) — Small hand-colored botanical drawing in the left column depicting a pink/red rose blossom with green leaves and a brown stem.

Elder tree (Von Blusen Khraft vnd Dugent des gemainen hollers) — Medium hand-colored botanical drawing in the right column depicting a leafy green elder tree with a brown trunk standing on layered brown-ochre ground.
Nettle sprig (Das khain har Wachse) — Small hand-colored botanical drawing in the right column depicting a leafy sprig (likely Urtica/nettle) with yellowish-green leaves.

Inkstand with quill pen (Guette Dintten Machen) — Small hand-colored drawing in the lower right column showing a cylindrical red-brown pot and a dark inkwell with a quill pen resting on a wooden desk.

Arum maculatum (Lords-and-Ladies / Cuckoo-pint) — Hand-colored botanical illustration in the upper-left margin of the right column showing three green leaves, a drooping bell-like flower in blue and yellow, and fibrous roots below.
Red-ink heart ornaments — Two small solid red-ink heart symbols centered beneath the rubricated headings 'In Hizigen frenen beÿ dem' and 'Ain Herliche Hertz Stärckung.' in the left column.
Red-ink wheel emblem — A small circular eight-spoked wheel or rosette drawn in red ink beneath the rubricated heading 'Zeltel für die Melancholischen Wind' in the right column.

Bust portrait of a young man in profile — Framed watercolor and pen-and-ink illustration in the left column beside the hair-loss recipes, showing a young man in profile facing left with wavy light-brown hair, wearing a red tunic with a wide yellow-ochre collar.

Soap-boiler at a furnace with a wooden lye tub — Framed watercolor and pen-and-ink illustration at the top of the right column depicting a man in a green tunic, black cap, and red breeches standing beside a brick hearth with a fire burning under a round cauldron, sprinkling powder while stirring with a rod; to the right stands a large hooped wooden tub on three legs.

Portrait bust illustrating Erbgrind (tinea capitis / scabby head) — Watercolor-tinted pen-and-ink bust of a boy or young man wearing a red-collared garment, resting on a rectangular plinth, depicting a mottled, scabby scalp condition (Erbgrind) above the corresponding section heading.
Small fluted vessel above Gall Tränckel — Small hand-drawn, blue-tinted conical cup or fluted vessel positioned above the 'Gall Tränckel' heading in the left column.

Tutia Alexandrina — Hand-drawn, washed illustration in grey and olive-green watercolor depicting a lumpy, layered mineral crust or nodule of Tutia Alexandrina (tutty / zinc oxide), positioned next to the rubricated heading 'Tutia Alexandrina' in the right column.

Two facing hands — Illustration in the right column between two horizontal olive-green/gold bands depicting two open human hands facing each other palm-inward, accompanying the text on how a physician should prepare his hands.
Würm — Framed rectangular illustration in the lower-middle left column with an olive-green/gold border containing wavy red-orange lines representing intestinal worms, labeled 'Würm' in red ink below.

Alchemical retort and flask — Two watercolor/ink drawings at the top of the left column above the Lutum Sapientiae heading: on the left, a brown-tinted round retort with a blue-tinted curved neck resting on a rectangular base; on the right, a round-bottomed glass flask with a long hatched neck resting on a rectangular stand; a cross '+' is drawn between them.
Smoking pipe — Drawing of a long-stemmed smoking pipe (tobacco pipe) in the lower-middle left column, just above the rubricated heading for herbal smoking tobacco.

Amputated human leg and foot — Colored anatomical watercolor/ink illustration at the top of the right column depicting a severed human lower leg and foot lying on mossy green-brown ground atop a rectangular cream-colored plinth, accompanying the section on cold gangrene (Vom khalten brandt).

Fumigation brazier and box — Ink and watercolor drawing on a wooden table or shelf showing a handled metal censer/brazier on a pedestal filled with glowing red coals and rising gray smoke, next to a closed cylindrical wooden or metal box.

Nasal suppository / rolled medicated plug — Watercolor and ink drawing of a cylindrical brown rolled plug or suppository (Zapffel) lying horizontally on a pale yellow-green surface next to the rubricated heading 'Zapffel in die Nasen'.

Crayfish / Crab Illustration (Cancer Symbol) — Hand-colored drawing in red and brown wash depicting a crayfish or crab centered below the rubricated heading 'Ein bad Miedl in Brust Krebs.', serving as a visual emblem for cancer (Krebs).

Seated Man at a Low Table with Basin — Large hand-colored illustration in the upper-left column depicting a bearded man in a red robe seated on a wooden bench, leaning forward with his hands over a shallow red-rimmed basin resting on a four-legged wooden stool; a stoneware jug and a small hand-broom sit beside the bench on a green ground.

Reclining patient figure (Right Column, middle) — Coloured ink and wash illustration framed in a ruled rectangle, depicting a figure draped in a red-and-white striped garment reclining on green ground with knees raised and bent, illustrating the posture for applying topical remedies or examining anal ulcers/fistulas.

Surgical instruments for exploring and cutting fistulas (two curved grooved directors/syringotomes, a bulbous probe, and a curved bistoury) — Pen-and-ink wash drawing of four surgical instruments arranged vertically in the right column: on the left, two curved, tapered grooved directors or fistula knives (syringotomes) shaded in brown wash; in the center, a slender dark-shaded probe with a bulbous, segmented handle at the bottom; on the right, a curved bistoury or scalpel with a dark, ornate handle and a curved single-edged blade.

Anatomical diagram showing fontanel (issue) placement sites on the human body — Pen-and-ink and watercolor drawing of a seated nude male figure seen from behind and in three-quarter profile, with his left arm raised and legs bent, resting on a rectangular wooden-style plinth. Von Stain sandt Vnd Jrieß — Hand-colored ink and watercolor illustration in the upper-left corner of the page depicting a bearded apothecary or physician with brown hair, dressed in a red doublet/coat with white cuffs, yellow-ochre breeches, and red stockings, leaning over a wooden table with glass alchemical flasks and vials (including a large round-bottomed flask filled with green liquid). Below the figure is a small landscape vignette with green grass, a brown bush/tree, and grey rocky ground.

Urine jug/flask and handled chamber pot on a wooden table — Centered in the right column above 'Den Verstopfften Vrin zu dreib'. On the right is a wide, low dark grey/black earthenware or pewter chamber pot with a single loop handle on the right side. Both vessels sit on a brown wooden table or shelf.

Urine flask (matula) on a wooden table with red urine symbol (⊡) — Positioned in the middle of the right column next to the rubricated heading 'Disuria Strangúgria Hernia harn.' A cylindrical blue-grey glass flask (matula) with a flared rim, narrow neck, and bulbous base containing golden-amber liquid, resting on a coiled yellow straw ring. Blank pasted label under 'Gonorrchea' — A blank, cream-colored rectangular paper slip framed in red ink, positioned directly beneath the rubricated heading 'Gonorrchea' in the upper-middle left of the right column, with a small ink dot near the center.

Anatomical diagram of the urinary bladder and urethra — A framed watercolor illustration in the middle of the right column depicting a rounded, orange-reddish urinary bladder with two sinuous/coiled ureters entering at the upper left and upper right, and a curved, tapering bladder neck/urethra descending downward to the right. Anatomical illustration of the urinary bladder — A hand-drawn anatomical illustration in red-brown ink and wash, framed in a square box in the upper-left portion of the right column beside the rubricated heading 'Von Geschwer der Blasen'. It depicts the urinary bladder as an ovoid sac with two sinuous ureters entering from the upper left and upper right sides, and a curved urethra extending downward and curving to the right.

Anatomical diagram of a urethral caruncle / bladder neck obstruction — A small hand-drawn anatomical illustration in brown and reddish-brown ink and wash, positioned in the right column just above the rubricated heading 'Weilen aber nach denen Geschweren'. It shows an ovoid bladder-like sac on the right tapering into a narrow horizontal canal/tube extending to the left, illustrating a fleshy growth (carnositides) or obstruction in the urinary canal.

Anatomical figure of a standing man wearing a hernia truss — Hand-coloured pen-and-ink wash illustration in the upper-left area of the page depicting a standing, beardless man with shoulder-length curly brown hair, naked except for a red and yellow sash/truss tied around his waist and groin (hernia bandage/suspensory). Unlabeled oval red-ink anatomical/hernia diagram — Small shaded oval/pear-shaped drawing in reddish-brown ink positioned to the left of the rubricated heading 'Volgen noch slüß mitl Vor die brüch' in the lower right column, depicting a swelling or scrotal/hernial sac.

(Unlabeled anatomical/surgical illustration showing a man with tumors) — A colored pen-and-ink and watercolor illustration in the upper half of the right column. (Unlabeled anatomical/surgical illustration showing a woman with a shoulder tumor) — A colored pen-and-ink and watercolor illustration in the upper portion of the right column. Kitchen/laboratory scene illustrating scalding and burns — Coloured ink-and-wash illustration in the upper-left column depicting a woman in a blue bodice, white apron, and red skirt standing in a doorway with her right hand raised in alarm, looking toward a brick hearth where a large cauldron hangs over a blazing fire from a chain and wooden beam, with pots, a ladle, and spilled liquid on the hearth and jars and pans on a shelf above.

Sympathetic healing and transplantation through a tree — Coloured ink-and-wash illustration in the upper-left column depicting a woman in a white headdress, red skirt, and white apron holding the outstretched hands/arms of a horizontal human figure passing through the trunk of a leafy green tree against a background of blue hills and sky.

Cichori Fluët. Ein herliche Reinigung des geblüets. — Colored botanical illustration in the upper-left corner of the left column depicting two plants growing from a grassy hillock: a smaller plant with blue flowers (chicory) on the left and a taller woody shrub or tree with red blossoms/leaves on the right.

Puluis Simpateticus, Wie es gemacht Und Gebraucht Wirdt. — Colored emblematic scene spanning the left column, framed by blue horizontal borders. Transplantation of disease into a dog and a tree — Colored watercolor and ink illustration in the middle of the right column. Four flowering wound-herbs (Wundkräuter) — Colored watercolor and ink illustration in the middle of the right column above the rubricated heading 'Anatomia der Wundt Kreidter.' Fluted glass flask (right column, beside 'Hundt Leben Machen') — A hand-drawn and painted illustration positioned on the left side of the right column alongside the rubricated heading 'Hundt Leben Machen Nim Grosse vnd Wunnderliche Wirckhung'. Maill Khugl — Two small shaded circular drawings of round balls or spheres (possibly medicinal or cosmetic soap balls) placed in the left column directly to the left of the rubricated heading 'Maill Khugl'.

Von der Glider Sucht. Arthritis — Colored pen-and-ink and watercolor illustration in the upper left column depicting a male patient suffering from gout/arthritis and a female attendant. — Anatomical illustration in blue wash and black/brown ink occupying the upper two-thirds of the left column, depicting a standing human figure on a green-brown grassy mound above a double blue horizontal border. Für dein Kranckheit ist khein Khraudt... — Colored ink and wash illustration of a bearded man suffering from gout (Podagra) seated in a wooden armchair. Der Khünigin Elisabeth in Ungern Von Gott geoffen bahrtes ▽ für das Podagra — Colored ink and wash illustration in the middle of the right column depicting a golden royal crown with a red velvet cap/lining and jeweled/ornamented rim, resting on a yellow-brown base.

— Color wash illustration in the lower-left quadrant showing a man in a pinkish-red tunic seated on a rectangular stone block, facing right in three-quarter profile with hands clasped over his chest and bare legs/feet resting on a dark greenish-brown sloped ground. — Color wash illustration in the upper-middle of the right column showing a white cloth draped over a shallow three-legged pan or brazier filled with glowing red coals/embers, resting on a yellow-ochre surface, illustrating a vapor/fumigation treatment for swollen feet.

— Color wash illustration in the lower-left of the right column showing a round wooden stave footbath tub bound with three horizontal hoops and filled with grey-blue liquid, resting on a yellow-ochre surface.

Cold tumor on the leg and foot (in 'Von denen khalten Tumoren an denen fießen vnd armen') — Colored ink and watercolor illustration placed in the lower-middle portion of the left column, showing a bare human right leg bent at the knee, resting on a green grassy mound. Ulcerated lower leg resting on a wooden footstool — Rectangular watercolor and ink illustration in the left column on a pale ochre ground depicting a bare lower leg from above the knee to the foot, resting horizontally with the heel supported on a small four-legged wooden stool and the thigh resting on a round wooden block. — Rectangular framed watercolor illustration in the middle of the left column depicting a bare human lower leg and foot resting the heel on a cylindrical wooden block on a greenish-yellow ground, with multiple reddish-brown circular lesions and ulcers along the shin and calf.

Anfang. — Rectangular watercolor illustration in the lower left column depicting a bare leg bent at the knee resting on a low yellow-ochre wooden block, with the lower leg tightly wrapped in a dark greyish-blue bandage and the bare foot extending to the right.

242 — Rectangular watercolor illustration at the bottom of the left column depicting a nude man lying on a yellow-ochre bed with a white bolster/pillow, his limbs and torso tensed in a convulsive spasm, with a dark backdrop and a brownish-green landscape to the right; numbered '242' in faint red-brown ink at the upper left of the frame.

Contractura. — Framed rectangular watercolor and ink illustration at the top of the right column, beneath the line 'Stirbt so stirbt der Patient —' and above the large rubricated heading 'Contractura.'. Anfang. / Von Schwinden der Glider — Colored pen-and-ink illustration in the lower-left column showing a half-length figure of a bearded man with shoulder-length brown hair, wearing a pinkish-red doublet with green-and-gold frogging/braiding and a white collar, standing behind a rectangular parapet or ledge. aufgehört. — Half-length watercolor-tinted ink portrait of a young woman facing forward/slightly left, with brown hair in a braided updo, wearing a red coral necklace, a laced red-and-grey/blue bodice over a white puffed-sleeve chemise, and raising her left hand with a red, black-spotted cuff. Ein anders der Graue Wolff genandt. — Colour-washed pen-and-ink illustration of a grey-brown wolf standing in profile facing left on a patch of ochre-green ground, positioned in the upper-left column beside the recipe ingredients for 'Der Graue Wolff'.

tz Puluär Gar kröfftig — Small painted reddish-brown oval diagram (representing a medicinal pellet or troche) placed inline between the two halves of the rubricated heading 'tz Puluär' and 'Gar kröfftig' in the right column.

Pointing hand (top of right column) — Colored ink and wash illustration at the top of the right column depicting a right hand with the index finger extended horizontally to the right, resting above a double horizontal blue/teal ink rule.

[Untitled illustration of a man afflicted with fistulas/lesions] — Rectangular watercolor illustration framed in red ink in the upper half of the left column. diser Vnder glich Instrumenta ~ — Large watercolor illustration occupying the lower half of the page, depicting seven surgical instruments for treating fistulas: two curved sickle-shaped bistouries/syringotomes with slender probe tips at the top; a straight probe/director with a turned dark wooden handle; a straight probe-pointed bistoury with a light brown wooden handle; a pair of surgical shears/scissors with looped spring-like handles; and three long-shafted actual cautery irons with turned wooden handles and variously shaped tips (triangular/hatchet, bulbous/olivary, and flat disc).

Patient suffering from fistulas/sores (above 'Von den fistlen des Vndern Leibs') — Watercolor illustration in the upper left column showing a figure with brown curly hair lying half-reclining on a wooden bed with white sheets and pillow, uncovered to the thighs, with numerous red spots/ulcers/fistulas across the chest, abdomen, arms, and legs. 435. — Watercolor illustration in the upper-left column showing a female patient reclining on a blue-and-white striped pillow, wearing a red cap and a grey garment open at the chest, with a bright red crab/lobster clinging to her left breast to symbolize breast cancer ('Krebs'). Instrumenta Welche Zu dieser operation gebraucht werden. — Full-column watercolor and ink illustration of surgical instruments used for breast cancer excision: two long-handled cautery irons with turned brown wooden handles (one with a rectangular flat plate head and one with a round disc head), a large broad-bladed surgical knife with a carved wooden handle, and two slender surgical needles/probes on the far right.

Anfang. — Framed watercolor illustration (blue and black ink border) depicting the lower body and bare legs of a person wearing reddish-brown breeches and holding a staff in the left hand, while a small brown dog bites the back of their left ankle, drawing bright red blood.
